goldens.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
goldens.reasoning: C1 points out the same non-atomic retryCount + 1 race condition.

goldens.comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
goldens.reasoning: C2 points out the same missing SMS method filter in the deleteMany OR clause, which deletes non-SMS reminders.

candidates: Using JavaScript-level addition (reminder.retryCount + 1) instead of Prisma's atomic increment operator creates race conditions when two scheduler instances run concurrently, causing one failure to be lost and weakening the delete after two failures logic
The second OR branch in the deleteMany query is missing a method guard, so it will delete any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, not just SMS reminders - the cleanup should be scoped to SMS only

The Twilio provider API call and database persistence are in a single try-catch, so if Twilio accepts the SMS but the database update fails, the error is treated as a send failure causing duplicate SMS on retry
After multiple database failures, the reminder row may be deleted leaving orphaned jobs on Twilio with no database reference
